item.title: [Idaho Capital Sun] Idaho budget committee introduces new health and welfare budget with additional cuts (3m)
item.description:
The Idaho budget committee has introduced a new health and human services budget that includes an additional $21 million in cuts to Medicaid disability services, following the rejection of a previous budget by the Idaho Senate. This reduction will not only impact essential services but also result in the loss of $44 million in federal funding, totaling a $65 million loss for the state. These cuts are part of a broader trend of budget reductions pushed by Idaho Republicans and the governor throughout the 2026 legislative session, raising concerns about the implications for vulnerable populations reliant on these services.

item.title: [Idaho Capital Sun] Idaho Legislature passes bill for Medicaid expansion work requirements by 2027 (8m)
item.description:
The Idaho Legislature has passed House Bill 913, which mandates work requirements for adults enrolled in Medicaid expansion, potentially leading to the removal of up to 44% of participants, or approximately 34,000 individuals, by 2028. Proponents argue that the bill ensures that those who can work are doing so, while critics contend that it imposes unnecessary barriers that could disqualify working Idahoans from receiving essential health coverage. This legislation is significant as it could undermine the Medicaid expansion approved by voters in 2018, which aimed to assist the working poor in accessing healthcare.

item.title: [Idaho Capital Sun] Trump signs order seeking to curb vote-by-mail in bid to control state election laws (2m)
item.description:
President Trump signed an executive order aimed at restricting mail-in voting by directing federal agencies to compile lists of voting-age citizens and requiring the U.S. Postal Service to implement tracking for ballots. This move signifies a significant attempt to assert federal control over elections, which are constitutionally managed by states, and reflects ongoing concerns about noncitizen voting, despite evidence showing its rarity. The order is likely to face legal challenges and raises questions about the implications for voter access and election integrity.
